newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: HK passport holders welcome after handover-Manila.
newsitem.headline: HK passport holders welcome after handover-Manila.

text.p: Hong Kong passport holders will continue to enjoy visa-free entry to the Philippines after the British colony returns to Chinese control on July 1, the Foreign Office said on Wednesday.
It said in a statement that the decision "manifests the confidence of the Philippine government in the ... continued stability and prosperity of Hong Kong beyond 1997."
Hong Kong is to become a Special Administrative Region (SAR) of China. Holders of SAR passports will be allowed to stay in the Philippines for seven days without visas.
Foreign Secretary Domingo Siazon conveyed Manila's decision to Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten and future chief executive Tung Chee-hwa, the Foreign Office statement said.

"By allowing visa-free entry for holders of each other's passports, our governments ensure that the substantial two-way flows of businessmen and visitors will continue to increase and that the relations between Hong Kong and the Philippines will continue to deepen and expand," it quoted Siazon as saying in his letters to the two officials.

"This is very good news coming so soon after the similar announcement by Canada and will further strengthen the trade, business and tourism ties between the Philippines and Hong Kong," Patten said in a statement.
Last week, the Canadian government announced it would continue to give visa-free access to Hong Kong passport holders beyond the handover.
Hong Kong people currently hold various documents, including limited British overseas passports that give no right of abode in Britain but allow visa-free entry to many countries.

Total trade between the Philippines and Hong Kong in 1996 exceeded $2 billion, with Hong Kong being the largest foreign equity investor in the Philippines that year, the Foreign Office statement said.
A total of 290,000 tourists from Hong Kong visited the Philippines in 1996, it added.
Siazon is scheduled to visit Hong Kong April 3-5 for talks with Patten, Tung and Finance Secretary Donald Tsang.
The passport issue and the welfare of more than 130,000 Filipinos, mostly domestic helpers, now working in the colony are among the matters Siazon will discuss with them, officials said.
Britain, Western Samoa and Singapore are the only other territories to have pledged visa-free entry for SAR passports.
